chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hafs Al-A'sha, from Amr [Umar] ibn Khalid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

I went out until I reached this wall and leaned against it, and behold, there was a man wearing two white garments looking at my face. Then he said, 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn, why do I see you as gloomy and sad? Is it over the world? For the sustenance of Allah is present for the righteous and the immoral.' I said, 'I do not grieve over this, and it is as you say.'
He said, 'So is it over the Hereafter? For the promise of Allah is true, and a Dominant King [or he said: All-Powerful] will judge in it.' I said, 'I do not grieve over this, and it is as you say.'
He said, 'From what is your grief?' I said, 'From what we fear from the strife of Ibn al-Zubayr and what the people are enduring in it.'

He laughed, then said, 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you seen anyone who supplicated to Allah but He did not answer him?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Have you seen anyone who relied upon Allah but He did not suffice him?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Have you seen anyone who asked Allah but He did not give him?' I said, 'No.' Then he disappeared from me.
ai.seo_question: What is the evidence for the reliability of Allah's response to supplication and reliance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) is consoled by a figure, widely interpreted by Shia scholars as the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) or the Mahdi (AJ), during the political turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr. The dialogue emphasizes the certainty of divine response to supplication and reliance (*tawakkul*), using a rhetorical triad to reassure the Imam that his anxiety over worldly strife is unfounded given Allah's consistent faithfulness to His servants.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hafs Al Ashay, from Amro Umar Bin Khali Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: 
‘I<sup>asws</sup> went out until I<sup>asws</sup> ended up to this wall. So I<sup>asws</sup> leaned against it, and there was a man upon whom were two white clothes, looking towards my<sup>asws</sup> face. Then he said, ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>! What is the matter I see you<sup>asws</sup> as bleak, aggrieved, is it upon the world? But, the sustenance of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is for the righteous and the immoral’. I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not upon this that I<sup>asws</sup> grieve, and it is just like you are saying’. 
He said, ‘So, upon the Hereafter? But the Promise is true. The King (Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>) has Judged with regards to it. The King, the Compeller’, or he said, ‘All-Powerful’. I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It is not upon this that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> grieve, and it is just like what you are saying’. 
So he said, ‘From what is your<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> grief?’ I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘From what we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> are fearing from the strife of Ibn Al-Zubeyr and what the people are indulging in’. 
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So he laughed, then said, ‘O Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! Have you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> seen anyone who supplicated to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, but He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> did not Answer him?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So have you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> seen anyone who relied upon Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, but He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> did no Suffice him?’ I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘No’. He said, ‘So have you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> seen anyone who asked Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, but He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> did not Give him?’ I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘No’. Then he disappeared’. 
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Mahbub from abu Hafs al-‘Asha’ from Amr ibn Khalid from abu Hamza al-Thumali from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once I walked out till I reached this wall and I leaned against it. At that time a man wearing only two pieces of white cloth was looking toward my face. He then said, ‘O, Ali son of al-Husayn (a.s.) you look very sad, as if you have suffered a great deal. Is it because of worldly things wherein the sustenance from Allah is available for all the good and bad people?’ I said, ‘I am not sad because of the worldly things; they are just as you said.’

He asked, ‘Is it then for the matters of the life hereafter, for which the promises will all come true? The Judge therein will be the forceful ruler,’ or he said, ‘Powerful ruler?’ I said, ‘This also is not the reason; it is just as you said it is.’
He then asked, ‘Why are you then so sad?’ I said, ‘It is because of the mischief of ibn Zubayr and the conditions of the people.’

The Imam said, ‘He then laughed and said, ‘O Ali son of al-Husayn (a.s.) have you ever come to know of anyone who prayed and Allah did not listen to his prayer?’ I said, ‘No, I have not known anyone as such.’ He then said, ‘Have you come to know of anyone who trusted Allah and He did not protect him?’ I said, ‘No (I have not found any such person).’ He then asked, ‘Have you come to know of anyone who asked Allah and he was not given anything?’ I said, ‘No (I have not found anyone as such).’ “The Imam said, ‘The man then disappeared from my sight.” Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub a similar Hadith.
